summary.text: A 22-year-old professional female futsal player in the Spanish First Division, with prior knee and ankle injuries that had not received psychological treatment, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament of her left knee on 1 October 2022 during a league match. Rehabilitation began on 11 October, and she underwent ACL reconstruction with a hamstring tendon graft on 14 November 2022.

Baseline psychological assessment at the initial evaluation showed mild depressive symptomatology on the BDI-II, trait anxiety at the 50th percentile and state anxiety at the 35th percentile, and perfectionism scores mostly above the 75th percentile with functional perfectionism above dysfunctional. She reported difficulty expressing emotions and emotional numbness during the initial interview, and the first printed pain catastrophizing total was 33 on 21 December.

A cognitive-behavioral psychological intervention ran from 13 December to 30 June in 15 sessions of about 50 minutes, covering goal setting, attention focusing, relaxation, sleep hygiene, problem solving, a letter to the injury, cognitive restructuring and visualization. Psychological assessments were repeated at follow-up, medical discharge and 3 and 6 months afterwards; meniscus surgery occurred during rehabilitation.

She was medically discharged on 1 August with a PRIA-RS score of 41 points, played her first official match on 12 September, and had no recurrence over six months of clinical follow-up. Pain catastrophizing fell from 33 to 8, DASS-21 scores stayed normal at follow-up, and the GHQ-12 score rose at 6 months, coinciding with a Super Cup defeat. She rated the intervention 9 for satisfaction.
